key_insight: The paper shows that in flow matching, different transport paths can produce the exact same training objective but very different SGD variance and convergence speed.
engineering_relevance: This means practitioners can potentially speed up diffusion/flow-matching training by choosing better paths without changing the target distribution or objective.
method: Analyze SGD gradient variance induced by different paths in the same FM family.
Derive an optimal path for a linear 1D Gaussian setting and a tight iteration-complexity bound.
Formulate PathOpt$_\theta$ with a sample-estimable reformulation for numerical path search.
evidence_signal: The theory is backed by experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: The variance-reducing path must satisfy the constraint $g_t\in G(p_t,v_t^\star)$; relaxing it can improve variance locally but actually slow convergence overall.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
